chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Muthanna al-Hannat, from 'Uyaynah, the seller of reeds, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: I enter the mosque on an intensely hot day, and I dislike praying upon the pebbles, so I spread my garment and perform sajdah upon it. He said: Yes, there is no harm in it.

key_terms.أَسْجُدُ: I perform sajdah, meaning I prostrate in prayer
key_terms.الْحَصَى: the pebbles or gravel on the mosque floor
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque, the place where the prayer is being performed
key_terms.الْيَوْمِ الشَّدِيدِ الْحَرِّ: a day of intense heat, describing the difficult circumstance
key_terms.ثَوْبِي: my garment, which is spread as a barrier
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: there is no harm in it, indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform sajdah on one's garment in extreme heat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning sajdah in conditions of severe heat. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام permits a person to spread his garment and perform sajdah on it in the mosque when praying directly on the hot pebbles is difficult.
